record.paper_title: Open Questions about Ramsey-Type Statements in Reverse Mathematics
record.context_brief: Minimal-degree solutions for EM or RWKL
record.original_question: Does every computable instance of the Erdős-Moser theorem, and even every computable instance of Ramsey-type weak König's lemma, have a solution of minimal Turing degree?

evidence.quote: Question 4.6 Does every computable EM-instance (or even RWKL-instance) admit a solution of minimal degree?
Construcing a similar model of EM would answer negatively Question 4.5. The following question is a first step towards an answer.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the framework of computability theory and reverse mathematics. A tournament on ω is an irreflexive binary relation T on ω such that for all distinct x,y ∈ ω exactly one of T(x,y) or T(y,x) holds. A tournament T is transitive if T(x,y) and T(y,z) imply T(x,z). The Erdős–Moser principle (EM) states: every infinite tournament on ω admits an infinite transitive subtournament. An EM-instance is an infinite tournament; a solution is an infinite transitive subset.

Ramsey-type weak König's lemma (RWKL) states: for every infinite binary tree T ⊆ 2^{<ω}, there exists an infinite set H ⊆ ω and a value c ∈ {0,1} such that for every n there is a path σ ∈ T of length max(H ∩ [0,n]) with σ(k) = c for all k ∈ H ∩ [0,n). An RWKL-instance is such a tree; a solution is such an infinite set H (with the associated color).

A Turing degree d > 0 is minimal if there is no Turing degree e with 0 < e < d.

Question: 
(a) Does every computable EM-instance admit a solution of minimal Turing degree?
(b) Does every computable RWKL-instance admit a solution of minimal Turing degree?
artifact.category_tag: reverse mathematics and computability of Ramsey-type principles
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of whether every computable EM- or RWKL-instance has a minimal-degree solution. Related work shows EM has no universal instance and that Δ⁰_n EM-instances admit low_{n+1} solutions, but the specific minimal-degree question for EM/RWKL appears not to have been definitively settled in the sources found.

status_evidence.title: The reverse mathematics of the thin set and Erdős–Moser theorems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies computability-theoretic strength of EM, including degrees of solutions, but does not record a resolution of the minimal-degree question.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the minimal-degree solution question for EM is reported.

status_evidence.title: Dominating the Erdős–Moser theorem in reverse mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Δ⁰_n instances of EM admit low_{n+1} solutions; EM does not admit a universal instance.
status_evidence.claim: Related computability results on EM solutions are known, but the minimal-degree problem is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: The weakness of the Erdős-Moser theorem under arithmetic reductions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2023) work on weakness of EM, focused on arithmetic preservation rather than minimal-degree solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature does not appear to settle the minimal-degree question.
